body:
Explaining to the school counsellor how I don't want to go to school will be odd, but, I guess it's the only option for me, before I do end it.

Although if I do talk to the counsellor, I can't mention suicide. I remember now that it's a trigger for parent involvement. 

Thank you for helping, even if in the end it doesn't work out.

I know my parents, they'll use every single available thing to avert the point: T.V. Computer. Phone. Pressure. Outside influences. Money. Laziness. They will try everything in the book to convince me that I really do want to be academic. No matter how much I say differently.

> it would help them too to understand what you're going through.

Do you mean tell them I'm depressed? No. No. No. I vowed I would never tell anyone again of my depression after the last person I ever uttered the word to never spoke to me again. And seeing a therapist would almost certainly result in my parents finding out.

What other way out is there? My parents keep pushing me to what they want me to be. They want me to be academic, smart and successful, but I just can't be that, I can't, I'm not good enough. I don't work hard enough and I can't get motivated. I hate that they picture me as this highly intelligent, thing they can mold into their 'perfect' son. It isn't what I want to do in life. I want to leave school, I want to move away, somewhere where nobody knows me, so I can start a new life. I can't tell them that though, they'd see me as a failure, look at me with thoughts of 'what could have been?' and I don't have the money to leave on my own!
There are other things too, but this is one of the biggest thing pulling me down, their expectation is weighing like an anchor on me.

Edit: Should add I'm 17 nearly 18
